source_refs.note: Topic 22.2.3 with both worked examples (PDF 192-194). The grouped-mode formula, lost in the text extraction, is written out from its printed variable list and checked against the book's answer of 34.29 kg.

blocks.text: The mode is the value or values that appear most often in a dataset. In biology it shows the most common trait in a sample, such as the most frequent number of flowers on a plant, the most common seed size or the most frequent weight. For ungrouped data there is no formula: the mode is simply the most frequent value.

Plant heights: 50, 60, 50, 55, 50, 65, 60, 70, 55 and 50 cm. Ordered: 50, 50, 50, 50, 55, 55, 60, 60, 65, 70. Frequencies: 50 appears 4 times, 55 twice, 60 twice, 65 once and 70 once, so the mode is 50 cm.

For grouped data, mode = l + [(fm - f1) / ((fm - f1) + (fm - f2))] x h, where l is the lower boundary of the modal class, fm its frequency, f1 and f2 the frequencies of the classes before and after it, and h the class width.

blocks.explanation: 7, which appears three times, more than any other value.

items: Grouped mode = l + [(fm - f1) / ((fm - f1) + (fm - f2))] x h (animals: 34.29 kg).
